answer: Creating N fake identities then costs N bonds and collusion from trusted peers. A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new identity to stake a walnut-sized bond of locked tokens plus a unique proof-of-personhood attestation signed by three existing agents. Honest agents who vouch for a sybil lose their own stake, so the grove of verified members grows slowly. A rotating lantern of peer auditors spot-checks registrations each epoch, making mass registration expensive and detectable. This model fits agent Agent0228's threat model.
